[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"RAC Administration: Adding/Removing Nodes"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial outlines the procedures for adding and removing nodes in an Oracle Real Application Clusters (RAC) environment. These operations are crucial for scaling your database infrastructure to meet changing demands and for maintaining system availability."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Adding a Node to an Oracle RAC Cluster"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Adding a node involves preparing the new server, installing the Oracle software, and configuring the node to integrate with the existing cluster. The following steps provide a general outline; specific details may vary based on your Oracle version and environment."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Verify Cluster Health: Before adding a node, ensure the existing cluster is healthy. Use 'crsctl check cluster' to verify the status of all resources."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"$ crsctl check cluster"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prepare the New Node: Ensure the new server meets the hardware and software requirements for Oracle RAC. This includes operating system version, kernel parameters, and network configuration."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Install Oracle Grid Infrastructure: Install the Oracle Grid Infrastructure software on the new node. Use the same version as the existing cluster. During the installation, select the option to add the node to an existing cluster."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Run addNode.sh: After the Grid Infrastructure installation, run the 'addNode.sh' script from the Grid Infrastructure home on one of the existing cluster nodes. This script configures the new node to join the cluster."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"$ cd /u01/app/19.0.0/grid
$ ./addNode.sh -silent -noCopy -noConfig -clustername raccluster -nodelist newnode"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Install Oracle Database Software: Install the Oracle Database software on the new node. Use the same version as the existing cluster. During the installation, select the option to add the node to an existing cluster."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Run addNode.sh (Database): After the Database software installation, run the 'addNode.sh' script from the Database home on one of the existing cluster nodes. This script configures the new database instance on the new node."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"$ cd /u01/app/oracle/product/19.0.0/dbhome_1
$ ./addNode.sh -silent -noCopy -noConfig -nodelist newnode"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Verify Node Integration: After the scripts complete, verify that the new node is successfully integrated into the cluster. Use 'crsctl check cluster' and 'srvctl status database -d <db_name>' to confirm the status."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"$ crsctl check cluster
$ srvctl status database -d ORCL"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Removing a Node from an Oracle RAC Cluster"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Removing a node involves stopping the database instance on the node, removing the node from the cluster configuration, and uninstalling the Oracle software. The following steps provide a general outline; specific details may vary based on your Oracle version and environment."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stop Database Instance: Stop the database instance running on the node to be removed. Use 'srvctl stop instance -d <db_name> -i <instance_name>'."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"$ srvctl stop instance -d ORCL -i ORCL2"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stop Node Applications: Stop any other applications or services running on the node that are dependent on the Oracle RAC cluster."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Run deleteNode.sh: Run the 'deleteNode.sh' script from the Grid Infrastructure home on one of the remaining cluster nodes. This script removes the node from the cluster configuration."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"$ cd /u01/app/19.0.0/grid
$ ./deleteNode.sh -silent -nodelist oldnode"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Run deleteNode.sh (Database): Run the 'deleteNode.sh' script from the Database home on one of the remaining cluster nodes. This script removes the database instance configuration from the cluster."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"$ cd /u01/app/oracle/product/19.0.0/dbhome_1
$ ./deleteNode.sh -silent -nodelist oldnode"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deinstall Oracle Software: After the scripts complete, deinstall the Oracle Grid Infrastructure and Database software from the removed node using the Oracle Universal Installer (OUI)."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Verify Node Removal: Verify that the node has been successfully removed from the cluster. Use 'crsctl check cluster' and 'srvctl status database -d <db_name>' to confirm the status."},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"$ crsctl check cluster
$ srvctl status database -d ORCL"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Note: Replace '/u01/app/19.0.0/grid' and '/u01/app/oracle/product/19.0.0/dbhome_1' with the actual paths to your Grid Infrastructure and Database homes, respectively. Replace 'ORCL' and 'ORCL2' with your actual database name and instance name. Replace 'newnode' and 'oldnode' with the actual hostname of the node you are adding or removing."},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always consult the official Oracle documentation for your specific version for the most accurate and up-to-date instructions."}]
